name: Red Squirrel Recovery Network Community Grants Scheme

administered_by.name: Red Squirrel Recovery Network (Northumberland Wildlife Trust)

summary: Micro and small grants for community groups and not-for-profits doing red squirrel conservation, including habitat improvement, in northern England and southern Scotland. Grey squirrel control costs are excluded.

geography.label: Northumberland, Cumbria, Scottish Borders, Dumfries & Galloway, South Ayrshire and parts of Lancashire/Merseyside

amount.note: Micro grants under £500, small grants £500 to £5,000.

reporting: Micro grants: a brief report and photos on outcomes and spending within 4 weeks of completion. Small grants: a detailed report with financial summary and photos after completion.

eligibility.rule: The project is located within the Red Squirrel Recovery Network area
The project benefits red squirrel conservation in line with RSRN goals
If an existing red squirrel volunteer group, applies for new activity only
The project excludes expenses related to grey squirrel control work

documents: Budget breakdown (small grants: detailed budget with all expenses and funding sources)
Proof of ownership if the project involves land, buildings or heritage items
Recent accounts or last three months of bank statements

administered_by.quote: Funded by The National Lottery Heritage Fund (TNLHF), the Red Squirrel Recovery Network (RSRN) is an ambitious five-year cross-border programme (2025-2030) working to prevent the extinction of the UK's native red squirrel (Sciurus vulgaris). The RSRN project is a partner collaboration; involving Northumberland Wildlife Trust (NWT), Cumbria Wildlife Trust (CWT)

applicant_types.quote: The Community Grants Scheme provides micro grants (under £500) and small grants (£500 to £5,000) to community groups and not-for-profit organisations.

geography.quote: the Red Squirrel Recovery Network area that covers Northumberland, Cumbria, Scottish Borders, Dumfries & Galloway, South Ayrshire and areas of Lancashire/Merseyside

access.quote: Submit the completed application form and budget breakdown online.

window.quote: Small Grants: Applications are reviewed quarterly.

amount.quote: it is unlikely the RSRN Community Grants Scheme will support grants larger than £5,000.

reporting.quote: A brief report and photographs detailing project outcomes and expenditure must be submitted within 4 weeks of project completion.

effort.quote: Submit the completed application form, detailed budget, and supporting documents online.

eligibility.quote: The project must be located within the Red Squirrel Recovery Network area that covers Northumberland, Cumbria, Scottish Borders, Dumfries & Galloway, South Ayrshire and areas of Lancashire/Merseyside which are a priority for red squirrels.

The project must benefit red squirrel conservation in line with RSRN goals i.e. by allowing more people to experience red squirrels, raising awareness about red squirrels, engaging more people in red squirrel conservation, enhance red squirrel habitat and increasing learning about red squirrels.
Existing red squirrel volunteer groups are eligible to apply for funding to support new activity only.
The RSRN Community Grants Scheme is not available for expenses related to grey squirrel control work as equipment for this is already provided through RSRN.

after_award.quote: A brief report and photographs detailing project outcomes and expenditure must be submitted within 4 weeks of project completion.

documents.quote: Budget Breakdown: Include a budget breakdown outlining how the grant will be spent.
Detailed Budget: Provide a detailed budget, including all projected expenses and funding sources.

the organisation's governing document proof of ownership if the project involves work to land, buildings or heritage items (for example, deeds, leases or any information relating to mortgages) copy of recent accounts or last three months of bank statements
